content.name: FIRS Industries 5
content.purpose: Primary industry replacement set — the source of the profile's deeper industrial chains.
content.notes: Defaults reviewed and kept — FIRS's own in-game economy selector (not a NewGRF parameter) is left at its default 'Basic' economy for approachability; see docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

content.name: Iron Horse 4
content.purpose: Primary train set, spanning 1860-2020 with FIRS-compatible cargo refits.
incompatibilities: economy.inflation = true (verified live: fatal NewGRF error, see docs/RESEARCH.md §5 'Stability check')
content.notes: Current actively-maintained generation (4), superseding the Iron Horse 3 originally suggested — see docs/RESEARCH.md. This profile's economy.inflation is kept at the engine default (false) specifically to avoid this conflict.

content.name: Road Hog (Buses, Trucks, Trams)
content.purpose: Road vehicle set (buses, trucks, trams) for the profile's road network layer.
content.notes: Feature-complete, unmaintained since 2018; still the strongest available FIRS-aware road set. Manifest 'name' deliberately uses the full BaNaNaS title (not just 'Road Hog') — the short form is a common substring that matches 50+ unrelated roadtype packages in `content state`, which was observed to make the filtered query dramatically slower; see docs/RESEARCH.md §3.

content.name: SHARK
content.purpose: Ship set for water-borne freight and passenger routes.

content.name: CHIPS Station Set 2
content.purpose: Industrial-freight-oriented station tiles built for use with sets like FIRS.
content.notes: Chosen over Industrial Stations Renewal (last released 2015) — see docs/MODS.md 'Deliberately excluded'.

content.name: OpenGFX+ Landscape
content.purpose: Landscape graphics enhancement for visual coherence with the rest of the stack.
content.notes: Loaded first — landscape/terrain graphics other GRFs may build on.

content.name: OpenGFX+ Trees
content.purpose: Tree graphics enhancement, paired with OpenGFX+ Landscape.

content.name: ITL Houses
content.purpose: Town/building visual variety and more realistic zoning behaviour.
content.notes: Loaded last — cosmetic house replacement, no cargo/industry interaction. Author states compatibility with all industry sets and Game Scripts.

content.name: Industrial Stations Renewal
content.omitted_reason: Overlaps CHIPS Station Set 2 for the same industrial-freight use case; last released 2015 versus CHIPS 2's 2021. See docs/MODS.md.

content.name: World Airliners Set
content.omitted_reason: No aircraft set showed sustained maintenance activity comparable to the rest of the stack, and aircraft is peripheral to the logistics profile's surface-transport focus. See docs/MODS.md.

content.name: U&RaTT
content.omitted_reason: Adds roadtype-selection complexity with no specific gameplay gap it fills for this profile. See docs/MODS.md.

content.name: Renewed Village Growth
content.purpose: Makes town growth depend on varied, sustained cargo delivery (including FIRS 5 cargos) rather than passenger-service spam alone.
content.notes: Verified compatible with FIRS 5 via the project's own current readme.txt — BaNaNaS's indexed search summary showed a stale 'up to FIRS 4.3' claim; see docs/RESEARCH.md §4. content_id is BaNaNaS's own canonical id (matches the downloaded tar's filename, verified live: 52455649-Renewed_Village_Growth-12.1.tar) — but the console's `content state` listing shows this same package's id byte-swapped (49564552). The installer tries both forms when matching a content_state row; see docs/RESEARCH.md §3.

content.name: RailwAI
content.purpose: Optional single AI opponent, installed only when the user explicitly opts in (--with-ai / -WithAI). Not installed or activated by default.
content.notes: Selected over AdmiralAI/CivilAI/SimpleAI after research (docs/RESEARCH.md §9): AdmiralAI is documented to break (repeated bankruptcy building airports) once infrastructure_maintenance is enabled, which this profile turns on by default; RailwAI's own description covers only trains/road vehicles/ships (no aircraft), sidestepping that whole failure class. More recently updated (2023) than CivilAI (2022, custom/unclear licence) and GPL-3.0 licensed. Not confirmed FIRS-specific-tested by its author, but OpenTTD's AI API is industry/cargo-set agnostic by design, so this is a reasonable, not a certain, compatibility bet — documented as such, not oversold. content_id is BaNaNaS's own canonical id (matches the downloaded tar's filename) — but the console's `content state` listing shows this same package's id byte-swapped (69617752, verified live). The installer tries both forms when matching a content_state row; see docs/RESEARCH.md §3.
